I searched `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, the module behind the generic `/ws/rest/v1` resources. Only two production classes there call `VisitService.saveVisit`, so a behaviour change would affect these:

1. **`VisitResource1_9.save(Visit)`** (line 253) returns `Context.getVisitService().saveVisit(visit)`. It is the `save` hook of the visit resource, so creating or updating a visit through REST goes through it.
2. **`VisitAttributeResource1_9.save`** (line 114) adds the attribute to its visit, then calls `saveVisit(delegate.getVisit())`. The attribute is persisted only through the visit, so a change in `saveVisit` affects it.
3. **`VisitAttributeResource1_9.delete`** (line 126) voids the attribute and calls `saveVisit(delegate.getVisit())`. The voiding is persisted only through this call.

Two test classes also call `saveVisit` to set up data: `VisitController1_9Test` (line 277) and `EncounterController1_9Test` (line 359). A behaviour change could break their setup.

I did not read the start of `VisitAttributeResource1_9.save`, so its method range starts at an approximate line (about 92).
